purpose: keep documentation accurate, findable and owned over time, so people can trust it
entry_criteria: A way to assign owners exists
A review cadence can be agreed
procedure: Inventory the documents, assign an owner to each and record the last review date.
Define standards for structure, naming, status labels and where each type of content lives.
Link documentation changes to code or process changes so they are reviewed together.
Review on a schedule by type, and archive or delete outdated pages instead of leaving them.
Check for broken links and orphaned pages automatically.
Track search failures and reader feedback, and fix the most common gaps first.
acceptance_criteria: Every document has an owner and a review date
No broken links in published docs
Changes to behavior include documentation updates

validation.check: list documents past their review date
validation.expect: each has an owner and a planned action

failure_modes.response: Tie docs to the change review

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: An inventory finds 12 pages with no owner. Eight are archived, four are assigned, and a link check runs in CI so a renamed page fails the build instead of leaving dead links.
